raw_response:
I’m old now, so I don’t chase fancy things. On my 5 mu, I’ll still do what has kept the family steady: keep most land in wheat-maize, and leave a smaller piece in cotton. Wheat and maize are the backbone here, and cotton gives me another way to earn if grain price is not so good. I only have 2 people at home, so I can’t spread myself too thin. I also have a well, so if it turns dry, I can still save the crop, but pumping water costs money, so I won’t irrigate carelessly.

For this year, I’ll put 3 mu in wheat-maize double cropping and 2 mu in cotton. Wheat is already on the land this season, so from now on I mainly watch water and topdressing. If the wheat stand stays decent, I’ll give one more fertilizer pass and 1 to 2 irrigations before harvest. After wheat comes off in June, I won’t waste time with heavy tillage, just a quick shallow till and sow maize fast, same as most people here. For cotton, I won’t put too much money into it, but I also can’t starve it, otherwise there is no boll. I’ll use the local seed people know, moderate fertilizer, and spray only when I really see pests or weeds. At my age, steady yield is better than gambling.
